## DISPLAY & VIDEO CAMPAIGN MASTERY

### Durable Setup Model
- Display and Video setups are asset-heavy and inventory-sensitive.
- The current specs guide is the canonical source for required text, image, logo, and video assets across responsive display and video-style campaign surfaces.
- Brand suitability and exclusions matter more here than in classic Search because inventory context changes where the ad appears.
- Google Display Ads campaigns are moving into Demand Gen: a migration tool rolled out from June 2026, the transition is expected to complete by 2027, migration carries settings and up to 42 days of history, and a migrated campaign can't be turned back. Google advises not migrating during a lift study. Demand Gen can still serve only on the Display Network.

### Normal Inputs And Controls
| Area | Typical concern |
|------|------------------|
| Assets | Image, logo, headline, description, business name, video coverage |
| Audience / targeting | Signals, targeting, exclusions, remarketing, current campaign-type-specific controls |
| Brand safety | Placement controls, exclusions, inventory suitability |
| Measurement | View-based and click-based outcomes, conversion setup, landing-page quality |

### Reporting / Diagnostic Surfaces
- Asset coverage, approval state, brand-suitability controls, conversion quality, and placement-context signals are the first checks.
- Current exact reporting detail is feature-sensitive. Corroborate current Google-owned Help wording if the user is asking what can be seen or controlled right now.

### What Not To Present As Fact
- Do not present old fixed recall-lift or intent-lift percentages as platform law.
- Do not imply that one universal video-sequencing recipe is a documented Google Ads rule.
- Do not flatten Demand Gen into generic Display or generic YouTube; use the "Demand Gen Setup" reference when the question is specifically Demand Gen.

## How to read this reference
- Sections titled "What Google documents" or "What Google-owned sources support" are **Official**: they restate Google pages listed below.
- Sections titled "Practical", "Discipline", "Operator" or "Workflow" are **Practitioner rules**: experience, not Google policy.
- "What Not To Present As Fact" lists claims to avoid stating as settled.
- Sources for this topic were last reviewed on 2026-10-14.
